subject: Rapid cooperation protocol: clarification on scope, timelines, and cross-border handling
body:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@apexbank.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, TrustBridge Legal <legal@trustbridge.co>
Cc: apex-security@apexbank.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible data exposure — ask re: timeline & subprocessors

Hi Laura / Redwood team,

We detected unusual outbound connections from a subset of customer-facing logs. At this stage we do not have evidence of exfiltration but need to confirm whether any Apex customer PII may have been involved. Per our DPA (section 7.2) we need:

- Confirmation of whether Redwood has a notifiable incident
- List of subprocessors that had access to the affected pipeline in last 30 days
- Expected timeframe for a scoped evidence export (we see 48h / 72h obligations in different clauses; please clarify what Redwood can commit to)

Can you also confirm whether evidence exports will cross borders (we have EU routing constraints for some customer datasets)? Attaching a redacted excerpt of our DPA for reference (Apex_DPA_excerpt.pdf).

We appreciate quick confirmation. If helpful, we can open a secure folder for evidence handoff.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Cybersecurity, ApexBank

-----

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@apexbank.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, trustbridge legal <legal@trustbridge.co>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — ask re: timeline & subprocessors

Hi Marta — thanks for the heads up and the DPA excerpt. We're treating this as high priority. Initial notes: 

- Redwood's standard notification commitment in our DPA is notification "without undue delay" and we operationalize that as a 72-hour internal triage-to-notify window for full-impact incidents. However, for limited-scope alerts (no confirmed customer data exposure) we often follow a 48-hour evidence-gathering cadence and provide interim updates.
- We will provide a current subprocessors list and call out any providers that had pipeline access in the last 30 days.
- Cross-border exports: we need to check whether the affected data was pinned to EU residency. If so, we'll route exports from our EU-resident export cluster; if not, the standard export path may traverse our US forensic cluster.

Action items I can own now:
1) Ben — scope a minimal evidence export (timestamped logs + redacted request traces) and estimate time-to-export. Please include a recommended data slice (by customer identifier and time window) and whether further quorum from Legal is required.
2) Kim — review the DPA excerpt and advise on any contractual levers (48h vs 72h, limited-forensic-access clauses) and note if we need an explicit mutual action plan.
3) Marta — please confirm whether Apex prefers EU-only handoff and whether a TrustBridge review can be used for access controls.

I'll loop Security (Grace) if Ben's triage finds anything beyond logs.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — ask re: timeline & subprocessors

Laura — quick triage update.

- Initial scan (retention logs + request traces) shows a short-lived increase in outbound POSTs from our ingest cluster between 2027-04-16T22:40Z and 2027-04-17T01:12Z. No obvious large payloads; payload sampling shows application-level telemetry (no raw customer content) in current samples.
- Subprocessors to flag: CDNCloud LLC (cache tier) and MirrorSync Analytics (usage telemetry). Both had pipeline-level access for the period in question.
- Export ETA: I can produce a scoped export (redacted request traces + delivery metadata) within ~36 hours if we do EU-only extraction from our Dublin cluster; full export from US forensics cluster is ~18 hours. The Dublin export requires additional encryption packaging (customer keys + HSM handoff) which adds steps.

Attachment: export_manifest_v1.csv (fields: customer_id_hash, start_ts, end_ts, data_type, residency_tag)

Recommendation: pursue EU-only handoff if Apex requires EU residency; otherwise prepare an interim report in 24 hours and a scoped evidence packet in 36 hours (EU) / 18 hours (US).

Ben Carter
Incident Response Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@apexbank.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, trustbridge legal <legal@trustbridge.co>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — ask re: timeline & subprocessors

Marta / Laura — legal perspective and proposed access controls.

Thanks for raising. A few legal/contractual clarifications:
1) DPA interpretation: the Apex excerpt points to a 48-hour interim update and a 72-hour substantive notification for material breaches. Contractually, we should:
   - Provide an interim statement within 48 hours confirming scope and whether customer data is impacted.
   - Provide a substantive report within 72 hours if material exposure is confirmed.
2) Limited forensic access: propose a mutually-executed access addendum (one-page) that specifies: allowed data slices, redaction requirements, export residency, and a 30-day retention limit for delivered evidence. I have a forensic_access_template.docx with suggested language.
3) Subprocessor disclosures: we can supply the standard subprocessors list plus a time-bounded access log for CDNCloud LLC and MirrorSync Analytics. If Apex needs proofs (SLA/SOC2 excerpts) we can surface those through TrustBridge.

Operational asks for Apex:
- Confirm preferred residency for exports (EU-only vs US).
- Confirm whether Apex wants a read-only view into our secure folder or prefers exported artifacts delivered to their secure binder.

If Apex confirms EU-only, Ben's estimate (~36 hours) for an export stands. If Apex accepts US export provenance, we can expedite to ~18 hours.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: forensic_access_template.docx

-----

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@apexbank.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: apex-security@apexbank.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — ask re: timeline & subprocessors

Laura / team — thanks for the clear plan. Apex prefers EU-only handling for the datasets we flagged. Two quick notes:

1) Please proceed with the EU-only scoped export and deliver the redacted evidence packet to the secure TrustBridge folder (send link and read-only permissions to security@apexbank.com).
2) We are comfortable with the proposed interim update at 48 hours and substantive evidence packet at 72 hours from your triage start. Please use April 19, 09:00 UTC as the triage start for our mutual action plan.

Next steps:
- Laura / Kim: please share the one-page access addendum for rapid signature (we can DocuSign).
- Ben: target the EU export in ~36 hours and confirm format (CSV + timestamped hashes).
- Grace / Redwood Security: please open a Zendesk incident and share the ticket id so Apex can reference it.

Acknowledged — Marta Ruiz
Head of Cybersecurity, ApexBank

-----

[End of thread]
